title: The Map on CarPlay
intro: OnMyLead 3.1 puts the map on your car's CarPlay screen, with turn-by-turn for the trail ahead, shows your trails and roads there with a Layers button to pick them, brings your ride's messages and group chats to the car, adds an Exit button to Map Mode and Ride Mode, makes Leave Ride easy to find, and turns Create a Ride into one short screen that opens already filled in. CarPlay is part of OnMyLead Pro.
whatsNew:
What's new in 3.1:

• The map on CarPlay: trails, your route, your group and turn-by-turn (Pro).
• Ride messages and group chats on CarPlay, with one-tap replies (Pro).
• Create a Ride is one short screen that starts on today, now and where you are.
• An Exit button in Map Mode and Ride Mode. Exit never leaves the ride.
• Leave Ride now sits right under the ride's name.
• Fixed a crash in Ride Mode. Zoom In at Intersections is now off unless you turn it on.

notes.text: CarPlay shows the OnMyLead map in your Map Style, turned so the way ahead is up: your position, the ride route and Leader Trackline, and every rider who is sharing, or in Map Mode the trail you follow and the one you're recording. During a ride, the rider line along the bottom shows everyone in running order, leader to tail gunner, with how far apart the group is. Zoom, recenter and pan from the car screen. Pro.

Trails and roads on the CarPlay map: off-road trails with their names, Forest Service and BLM roads and trails, dirt and paved roads, hiking trails and closures, from your Map Features. Tap Layers on the car to turn them on and off; your picks are saved for every map in the app.

Turn-by-turn on CarPlay while you follow a trail or the ride route: the next turn with an arrow and how far away it is, the turn after it, and the arrival, with miles and time left. The turns come from the trail's own shape, so they work on any trail. Before the trail, the car points you to its start; for road directions there, use Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps.

Messages on CarPlay: the ride's latest messages with who sent them and when. Tap one to hear it read out, and tap Reply to send a quick reply, including your own saved My Quick Replies. Your group chats are there too, during a ride and without one. While your phone shares on a ride, Open Ride Mode on the car opens Ride Mode. There's no typing in the car.

An Exit button at the top left of Map Mode and Ride Mode (and in the Full Map bar), plus Android's Back button and Exit on the CarPlay screen. Exiting Ride Mode keeps you on the ride; it asks first if you're sharing your location, and Map Mode asks first if you're recording a trail.

Events is now Events and Group Rides. A switch at the top shows public events, public group rides near you (the same rides as the Rides tab, nearest first, with the distance chip) or your own events, and Create makes a public ride while you're on Group Rides. The Home tile is renamed to match; the tab bar keeps the short name Events.
Fixed Ride Mode closing by itself during a ride when the phone couldn't save part of your ride track: it no longer retries over and over.
Zoom In at Intersections is now off unless you turn it on, in Map Settings under Following or in You under On the Trail. If you had turned it on, it stays on.

Leaving a ride is easier to find. The ride page shows where you stand right under the ride's name (You're Going, You're Riding, Request Sent, You're on the Waitlist or You're Organizing) with Leave Ride, Withdraw or Leave Waitlist beside it, instead of at the bottom of the page. It always asks first, and organizers pick who takes the ride over before they go.

Exit in Ride Mode always offers Leave Ride at the bottom of its box, under Done with this ride?, even when you aren't sharing your location. Exit Ride Mode is still the big button, and Android's Back button still closes Ride Mode straight away when you aren't sharing.

Create a Ride is one short screen that opens already filled in: today, the next quarter hour, where you are (when location is allowed), and a ride for the friends you invite. A ride from here, right now, is two taps: Start a Ride, then Create. Nothing is required but a meeting point.
Day and Meet At are plain fields. Tap the day and a calendar opens; tap the time and a list of times opens, every 15 minutes. Picking closes it.
Your last three named meeting points show as buttons under Meeting Point, so your usual gas station or trailhead is one tap. They're kept on your device.

The ride name is optional (an empty name becomes the day, like "Saturday Ride"). Who Can Join starts on Friends I Invite and then on what you picked last time, and the vehicles welcome start on your last ride's.

The vehicles welcome, rider limits, your own invite code, riding groups and the ride's details moved under More Options. Mapped or Freeride stays on the main screen: it starts on Freeride and then on what you picked last time.

title: Follow Me Fix for Map Mode
intro: OnMyLead 3.0.1 is the first store release of 3.0, with everything in 3.0 below, and it fixes Follow Me in Map Mode: the map now moves before your dot slides under the bottom panel.
whatsNew:
What's new in 3.0.1:

• A new look: Map Mode up front, five tabs, a Home you can customize, and bolder Rides, Events, Social and Ride Mode.
• Make It a Group Ride, right from Map Mode (Pro).
• Invite your riding group to an event.
• Starlink status on Home.
• Crop photos before they upload.
• Smoother Zoom In at Intersections.
• Show Password in every password box.
• CarPlay works in Map Mode (Pro).
• Ad Measurement: you choose.
• Fixed: CarPlay and 3D Terrain crashes, and Follow Me in Map Mode.

notes.text: Map Mode: with Follow Me on, the map now reacts when your dot gets close to the bottom panel. It zooms out one step the first time, then centers on your dot and moves with you. Before, the map waited until your dot was already hidden under the panel.

title: A New Look, Map Mode Up Front, Invite Your Group to an Event and Show Password
intro: OnMyLead 3.0 is a new look. Home opens on a satellite map of your area with Map Mode first, because OnMyLead is now your offroad map whether you ride solo or with a group. Join a Ride, Start a Ride and Events sit right under it, and you choose and order the rest. Map Mode tells you when you're riding solo, and Pro riders can turn that ride into a group ride in two taps. Event hosts can now invite a whole riding group in one tap, just like on a ride. It smooths out Zoom In at Intersections: when junctions come close together, like riding through town or a web of trails, the map now stays zoomed in from one to the next instead of zooming out and straight back in. Every password box now has an eye button so you can check what you typed before you tap Sign In. CarPlay now works on solo rides too: open Map Mode and the car screen shows your speed, elevation, heading, trip and the trail you're following. When you're on a Starlink's Wi-Fi, Home now shows its speed, latency and how many devices are connected. Every photo you add, from your profile picture to event and trail photos, now opens on a crop screen so you can frame it first. And it fixes a crash on iPhone when the app opened while your phone was already connected to CarPlay.
whatsNew:
What's new in 3.0:

• A new look: Map Mode up front, five tabs, a Home you can customize, and bolder Rides, Events, Social and Ride Mode.
• Make It a Group Ride, right from Map Mode (Pro).
• Invite your riding group to an event.
• Starlink status on Home.
• Crop photos before they upload.
• Smoother Zoom In at Intersections.
• Show Password in every password box.
• CarPlay works in Map Mode (Pro).
• Ad Measurement: you choose.
• Fixed: crashes with CarPlay connected and in 3D Terrain on Android.

notes.text: A new look: Home opens on a satellite map of your area. Map Mode comes first, then the red Join a Ride card with the code box, then Start a Ride and Events. Under them: Out Riding Now, Up Next (your invites, next ride and next event), Your Group and your Feed. Headings are in Title Case and every card has a clear edge.

Customize Home: tap Customize Home at the bottom of Home to turn sections on or off and move them up or down, including Public Rides Near You and Past Rides. Your badges and rank sit at the very top, just above your greeting, and Your Toolkit is always at the bottom. Your layout follows your account to every phone, tablet and the website.

Five tabs: Home, Rides, a raised blue Map Mode key in the middle, Events and Social. Riding Groups are inside Social, and You opens from your picture at the top of Home. On a tablet the tabs sit in a rail down the left with You at the bottom.

Starlink on Home: when you're on a Starlink's Wi-Fi, Home shows a Starlink card with whether the dish is online, download and upload speed, latency, how much sky is blocked and how many devices are connected. It's only there while a Starlink is connected. Tap it for the full Starlink page.

Bolder screens everywhere: Rides Near You shows each ride as a card with a map picture, the day, how far it is and its difficulty. Events leads with the next event as a big photo with I'm Going and Share right on it, and Create moves to the top right. Social opens with your Riding Groups and a row of friends, with a green ring on anyone out riding. In Ride Mode the status buttons are bigger, Mechanical Issue and Need Help sit on the panel, and EMERGENCY is a solid red bar in the same spot every time.

Riding solo in Map Mode: a Solo tag at the top says nobody else sees where you are. Pro riders tap Make It a Group Ride to turn the trail they're following or recording into a group ride, with where they are as the meeting point, then invite riders with a code.

Invite a Group on events: an event's hosts and co-hosts tap Invite All next to a riding group on the event page. Everyone in the group gets a notification that opens the event, where they can tap Going or Interested. Riders who already answered or were already invited aren't notified again.

CarPlay in Map Mode: with no group ride running, open Map Mode on your iPhone (or tap Open Map Mode on the car screen) and CarPlay shows Speed, Elevation, Heading, Trip and Moving time, the miles left on the trail you're following, and Pause or Resume for a recording. The map stays on your phone. Part of OnMyLead Pro.

Zoom In at Intersections: once you're through a junction, the map looks about a quarter mile ahead. If another junction is coming, it stays zoomed in for that one too, and zooms back out once after the last one, so the map no longer pumps in and out in town or on a web of trails.

Show Password: the password boxes on Sign In, Create Account and New Password have an eye button at the right edge. Tap it to see what you typed and tap it again to hide it. The password starts hidden every time.

CarPlay: opening OnMyLead on your iPhone while it was already connected to CarPlay (or changing Dark, Light or Match Phone while connected) could close the app. It now opens normally and the car screen keeps working.
3D Terrain on Android: the app could close while the 3D Terrain map was showing, for example when tilting the map or switching map styles. It now keeps running.

Ad Measurement: OnMyLead now asks once, on iPhone and iPad with Apple's tracking prompt, whether Meta and TikTok may learn that one of our ads brought you here (an install, a new account, a trial or a Pro purchase). It never includes your location, rides, messages or email. Say no and nothing is sent. On Android it's a switch in You > Settings > Ad Measurement, and onmylead.com asks before loading any ad cookies.

Crop any photo before it uploads. Your profile picture, group photo, machine photo, post photo, event photos, trail photos and bug report screenshots open on a crop screen first: drag the photo, pinch or double-tap to zoom (or use the minus and plus buttons), and tap Use Photo. Profile pictures crop square with a circle guide, group photos wide (16:9) and machine photos 4:3; for the rest pick Original, Square, 4:3, 16:9 or 4:5. Adding several event photos crops them one by one, or tap Use the Rest As They Are. Group photos on iPhone and iPad are no longer cut to the middle for you. It works the same on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and tablets, and onmylead.com, where the mouse wheel and keyboard zoom and move the photo too.
How Did You Find OnMyLead?: new riders see one quick question on Home, asked once. Tap where you heard about us or tap Not Now. Answers are only counted, never shown to other riders.
Post photos keep their shape: a tall or wide photo in a post now shows as you took it (from portrait 4:5 to wide 16:9) instead of being cropped to the same box every time.
Make It a Group Ride sets the meet time to the next quarter hour today, so a ride you start from the trail is ready to go now instead of at 8:00 am.
Android: the fades on the Home cards showed as solid black. They now fade like on iPhone. Map Mode's Center on Me, Follow Me and music buttons also stay above the bottom panel on every phone size.

title: Bluetooth Sharing With No Service, Every Map on Mapbox, 3D Terrain and the Badge Leaderboard
intro: OnMyLead 2.1 keeps your group talking where the signal ends: with no cell service, riders on the same ride pass spots, status taps, EMERGENCY alerts and messages to each other over Bluetooth, phone to phone, and every phone passes them along the group (seeing riders and sharing over Bluetooth is part of OnMyLead Pro; on every plan your phone passes alerts along and EMERGENCY goes out, and every rider without Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial with this update). When a rider sends EMERGENCY or their Crash Alert goes out, every other rider's phone now sounds a loud siren until they silence it. The new Leaderboard ranks riders by the badges they earned by riding. 3D Terrain is a new map style for Ride Mode and Map Mode that shows the real shape of the land, so you can see the ridges, canyons and climbs ahead. And every map in the app is now drawn by Mapbox, so Ride Mode, Map Mode, the route builder and Find a Ride look and work the same on your phone, tablet and onmylead.com.
whatsNew:
What's new in 2.1:

• No service? Bluetooth Sharing keeps your group talking: spots, taps and messages (Pro) and EMERGENCY (every plan) go phone to phone, rider to rider.
• Emergency Siren when a rider sends SOS.
• New rider dot; leader blue, tail gunner violet.
• Leader Trackline.
• Map zooms in at intersections.
• Edit Ride Details anytime.
• Badge Leaderboard.
• 3D Terrain, offline too.
• Hold the map to drop a waypoint.
• Map Settings: style, roads, trails, land.
• CarPlay (Pro).

notes.text: Bluetooth Sharing: when there's no cell service, Ride Mode passes your spot (while you're sharing with the ride), your status taps, EMERGENCY, quick replies and typed messages to nearby riders on the same ride over Bluetooth, about 100 to 300 feet between phones, and every phone passes along what it hears, up to six phones down the line, so the back of the group can reach the front. Phones that get a newer spot for any rider pass that on too, and a phone with signal shares what OnMyLead knows with the riders near it that have none. The card under your tap says whose phone got it over Bluetooth and who has seen it, even while it waits for signal. Messages heard over Bluetooth show in chat marked Via Bluetooth. When any phone on the ride gets signal, it sends what it heard so everyone else sees it too. Everything is encrypted for your ride only, and the radio idles when you have service and nobody is in range. Seeing riders and sharing your spot, taps and messages over Bluetooth is part of OnMyLead Pro (and the Pro Trial); on every plan your phone passes everything along, and EMERGENCY, Need Help and Crash Alerts go out over Bluetooth. Turn it off any time on the You tab.

New in Pro: Bluetooth Sharing with no service (EMERGENCY, Need Help, Crash Alerts and passing things along stay free), CarPlay, customizing your dot (Dot Style and Dot Size) and adding group photos. Everyone can still see group photos, and on Free your dot is the Red, White and Blue dot. So nobody loses anything the day 2.1 arrives, every rider who doesn't have Pro gets a fresh 30-day Pro trial, even if you had one before, and Home shows the date it ends. Safety stays free on every plan.

Group Spread on the leader line: a thin measuring line under the rider dots runs from the leader to the tail gunner, with how far back the last rider is in the middle (such as 0.8 mi) and small ticks every round step, so you can see how far apart the group really is. It works on routes and Freerides, and with Bluetooth Sharing when there's no service. The big miles-done number above the line is gone, and the line about your place is centered under it.

Emergency Siren: when another rider on your ride sends EMERGENCY, from the button, CarPlay or a Crash Alert that ran out, your phone sounds a loud siren on a full-screen alert until you tap Silence Siren or Show Me Where. With OnMyLead open it plays even with the ring/silent switch on silent and turns your music down under it; with the app closed the notification itself plays the siren (on Android as an alarm, so you hear it with the ringer on silent). With no service it sounds over Bluetooth too. It stops by itself if the rider cancels or taps I'm OK. It's on for everyone; switch it off or tap Play Siren to hear it in Notification Settings.

A new rider dot with the arrow built in: every live rider is a glossy disc with a white rim and a white arrow pointing the way they're heading, and it keeps pointing their last way while they're stopped. The leader is the biggest dot, in blue; the tail gunner is next, in violet; everyone else is graphite. Your own dot is big (Red, White and Blue unless you pick another Dot Style) with a soft beam ahead of it, and its arrow always shows which way you're facing: the way you're riding while you move, your phone's compass when you stop.

Map Settings: the round Map Settings button on the map opens one sheet for everything about the map. Pick Satellite, Topo or 3D Terrain from pictures of each, flip big switches for Streets and Roads, Off-Road Trails, Hiking Trails and Land Boundaries (or fine-tune every map feature), choose how the map follows you (Follow Me, Zoom Out at the Edge, Zoom In at Intersections), pick your own dot's look and size (a red, white and blue 3D dome by default), and turn the Tilt Meter and Music button on or off. The button sits in the top-left corner of every riding map, level with the compass on the right, just under the top bar so nothing covers them, and both stay on screen in Full Map. On a tablet held sideways the sheet sits beside the map so you see each change as you make it.

The map moves smoothly while you ride. Your own dot glides in step with the map again instead of trailing it, and the map does less work every second, so it keeps up when you're moving. If a map lookup ever stalls, the map still keeps your dot on screen, and the app's own map moves no longer pause Follow Me.

The map keeps your dot on screen: your dot moves through the middle of the map, the map zooms out one step the first time you get within about a tenth of the screen of an edge, and the next time it centers on your dot and moves with you so you never ride off the screen. Center on Me starts that over.

Leader Trackline: in Ride Mode a line in the leader's blue follows behind the leader on every rider's map, so at a fork or a faint trail you can see exactly which way they went. When the leader crosses the line, rides a loop back to the start or doubles back down the same trail, the older pass fades to a thin dashed line and the fresh line stays bright on top. The leader can turn it off for everyone from the layers button. Also on onmylead.com's live map.

Zoom In at Intersections: while the map follows you, it zooms in as you come up on a junction of roads or trails so you can see the turn, then zooms back out once you're through. On by default; turn it off in the You tab under On the Trail.

Scout: find places to ride. Tap Places to Ride at the top of the Find tab to see off-road parks, OHV areas, trail systems, trailheads and motocross tracks around you, 250 miles out to start; slide the distance anywhere from 10 to 1,000 miles. Filter by kind, tap a place for directions, its website and the public rides coming up there, or tap Create a Ride Here to start one with the meeting point already set. Places come from the Forest Service, BLM and OpenStreetMap, and you can suggest one we're missing. Also on onmylead.com.

Offroad park trails on every map: the trails of Hidden Falls Adventure Park, Katemcy Rocks, Wolf Caves, General Sam's, Hollister Hills, Hungry Valley, Ocotillo Wells, Interlake, SMORR, Sand Mountain and about fifty more parks and OHV areas, from OpenStreetMap, drawn for everyone. Where the park rates its trails, each line takes the park's level color (green 1-2, blue 3, white 4, red 5) and closed trails show as red dashes; park names sit on the map from far out with how much is mapped, trail names appear as you zoom in, and a tap shows the park, the trail's level and its length. A park you've looked at draws again with no signal. Turn Park Trails off in the layers panel or on the You tab.

Every map in the app is now drawn by Mapbox: Ride Mode, Map Mode, the route builder, waypoints, Find a Ride and Offline Maps' area picker, on iPhone, iPad, Android and onmylead.com. A map looks and works the same wherever you open it, and the website's Ride Mode now shows the same live map as the phone. Free accounts get Mapbox's outdoors map with roads, trails and contours. The meeting-point map is on the phone and tablet too, a trail's page previews it on a real map, and in 3D Terrain tilting further raises the land.

Faster trail lines: when you zoom in, roads and trails show up much sooner. The map asks the Forest Service and BLM for a quarter as many map pieces, Mapbox draws OpenStreetMap tracks and their names itself as you pinch, and trail names, closures and rider trails start loading as soon as the map stops moving. BLM routes show again too: BLM moved its route map to a new address, which had kept BLM lines off the map.
A 3D button on the map in Ride Mode and Map Mode: one tap tilts the map into 3D Terrain, another lays it flat again in the style you had. It stays on the map in Full Map too.

Map Features: the map layers panel now lists every kind of line and land the map can show, each with a picture of how it looks, to turn on and off. Highways and freeways are heavy blue lines and paved public roads lighter blue, so they never look like trails. Dirt roads are white, Forest Service roads open only to street-legal vehicles are lavender, trails limited to 50-inch machines or dirt bikes are orange, and hiking trails are a thinner pink dash-dot, so you can tell at a glance where you can't ride. Turn on National Forests, BLM Land, National Parks, State Parks and, in Texas, Property Lines, then tap the map to see whose land you're on and whether it's open to the public. Your choices follow you to your other devices.

Swipe the panel down to go full screen: a long swipe (or a quick flick) on the panel in Ride Mode, Map Mode, the route builder and Waypoints goes straight to Full Map, and a swipe down on a folded panel does too. A small grab bar at the bottom swipes up to bring everything back.

Edit Ride Details: the organizer or a co-organizer can change a ride's name, day, times, meeting point and details after creating it, from the ride page on the app and onmylead.com. Everyone on the ride gets a notification about a new time or meeting point, and the ride page shows what changed for a week. Once the ride is live, the day, times and meeting point are locked and the rest can still change.
Continue with Apple on Android and at onmylead.com, through Apple's web sign-in, once it's switched on. It signs you into the same account as Apple on your iPhone.
Presented by RUS Offroad: events that RUS Offroad presents show it in gold on their card and page, with a Shop RUS Offroad button.

Badge Leaderboard. Open it from Badges or from Your Badges on Home to see riders ranked by the badge levels they earned by riding, with Gold and then Silver breaking ties. Filter by country, then by state or province in the United States, Canada, Mexico and Australia. Pick where you ride from (Use My Location fills it in on your phone and saves only the country and state), and turn off Show Me on the Leaderboard any time to leave it. On a tablet your place and the filters sit beside the board.

3D Terrain: pick it under the map layers button in Ride Mode and Map Mode to see satellite on the real shape of the land, with contour lines and peak heights in feet. Drag with two fingers to tilt, twist to turn. Riders, your route, waypoints, trails and the distance finder all show on it.
Offline Maps can save 3D Terrain with an area or a ride, so the 3D map works where there's no signal. The download size shows before you start.

Press and hold the map in Ride Mode or Map Mode to drop a waypoint right there, then tap it to edit or remove it. On a group ride the leader's waypoints are shared with everyone, and the other riders' phones ding with "Lou added a new waypoint: Fuel Stop". Tap it to see the waypoint in Ride Mode. In Map Mode on your own, waypoints are yours, saved on your phone for no-signal riding and synced to your other devices with Pro.

Home fits on one screen: Join a Ride, Create a Ride, Find a Ride, Events and Map Mode are all on the first screen without scrolling, with Events right under Create and Find. The cards are shorter, and Track Line is a small switch in the corner of the Map Mode card.

CarPlay: plug your iPhone into a CarPlay car (or connect wirelessly) during a ride and OnMyLead shows on the car screen. One tap sends OK, Stopped, Need Fuel, Mechanical Issue or Need Help to the group, Regroup Here (organizer and leader) or Running Late, and EMERGENCY asks once before it alerts everyone. Group lists every rider, and the leader and tail gunner get an alert on the car screen when someone falls behind. Open Ride Mode on your phone first; the car screen follows it.

Share Picture works with Facebook, Instagram and Messages again: the shared card is now a 1080 pixel picture named OnMyLead, a couple of MB at most, instead of a 40 MB file the other app couldn't take.

Trail names follow their own switch in Map Features: Off-Road Trails names with Off-Road Trails, hiking path names with Hiking Trails. A park's miles count its trails only. Rider Trails and Park Trails switched on in the You tab show on every map again.
Opening a comment or the Activity feed right as the app comes to the front no longer shows an error: the request is tried again quietly, and if there is still no signal you get a Retry button.

Like and reply to comments: every comment in Social has Like and Reply. Replies sit under the comment they answer, and the rider you answer or whose comment you like gets a notification. Liking is free; replying is part of commenting, so it's Pro. A friend's post with a photo now shows the photo right in the Feed on the Rides tab.
Posts, comments and chat messages show exactly as the rider wrote them in every language, and reward dates show in your language.
A new waypoint alert goes out once per waypoint: switching it to Just Me and back no longer alerts the ride again.
Refer a Friend: your friend's first ride counts once that ride has actually started, so a ride that was created and never led doesn't earn the reward.

Group Photos: the rider who made a riding group can take or choose a photo for it, change it or remove it, from Group Photo on the group page. It shows wide at the top of the group page (tap it to see it full size), next to the group's name on Riding Groups, on the Your Group card on Home and under Invite a Group on a ride, and at the top of the group's invite link, on the website too. Groups without one show their initials. On Android you frame it on the crop screen; on iPhone, iPad and the website the middle of the photo is used.

Always call 911 in an emergency: the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement (version 2) now says plainly that EMERGENCY, Crash Alert, Need Help and the Emergency Siren only alert riders on your ride and never call 911 or a rescue service. After you update, the Before You Ride screen shows once more so you can read it and tap I Agree.
See which version you have: the very bottom of Home shows it with the build number, like Version 2.1 (10), and it shows on the logo screen for a moment when the app opens.

title: A New Home, Social, Events and Map Mode
intro: OnMyLead 2.0 is the biggest update yet. A new Home screen puts Join a Ride, Create a Ride and Find a Ride up front, with public rides near you, your group, your badges and a Feed of what your friends have been riding. Social lets you like and comment on your friends' rides, badges and trails, post ride reports with a photo and see any rider's profile. Events brings rallies, poker runs and ride weekends to one page with their agenda and group rides. Navigate is now Map Mode, with custom trails, a Track Line of where you've been and named spots like water crossings. A Tilt Meter shows your roll and pitch, and Crash Alert starts an I'm OK countdown after a hard hit or rollover before it alerts your group. Founder and Brand Ambassador badges join the badges, and your trails and settings sync across your devices. You can pick Light or Dark, four themes and a Color Blind Mode, and the app now speaks 12 languages. Ride Mode is cleaner and smoother, with your own typed messages, a Beverage Break quick reply, Follow Me, Full Map and Music Controls. Invite a friend who's new to OnMyLead, and when they finish their first ride you both get Pro Annual at half price for the first year. And there's a notifications inbox, easier Leave Ride, better handling of rough locations, Report a Rider, a Rider Safety Agreement, gold Pro tags, new Free and Pro plans (joining a ride and following the leader stay free and unlimited, and Map Mode is free for 8 hours a month) and ride miles that match the ride, and trails now show width limits so you know your machine fits.
whatsNew:
What's new in 2.0:

• New Home with a Feed of your friends' rides.
• Social: like, comment and post.
• Events: rallies and ride weekends.
• Map Mode: custom trails, Track Line.
• Tilt Meter and Crash Alert.
• Smoother Ride Mode, Full Map, Follow Me.
• Light mode, 4 themes, Color Blind Mode.
• 12 languages. Sync across devices.
• Invite Friends: both save 50%.
• Founder and Ambassador badges.
• Trail width limits, waypoint symbols.
• Notifications bell, Music Controls.
• New Free and Pro plans.

notes.text: A new Home screen. Join a Ride sits at the top with a box for the invite code, next to Create a Ride (with the rides you have left this month) and Find a Ride (with how many are near you). Below them: your next ride, your riding group with its latest message, Public Rides Near You (choose 50 to 1,000 miles or Anywhere, 500 to start), your Feed, your badges and Your Toolkit with Garage, Starlink, Battery Saver and the rest. On a tablet it uses two columns.

Your Feed on Home shows what your friends, the leaders you follow and your riding groups have been up to in the last 30 days: rides they finished, badges they earned, trails they shared and group rides they posted. Tap Customize to choose whose posts and which kinds you see. Nobody's location is ever shown.

Social: like and comment on your friends' rides, badges, trails and posts, post a ride report with a photo on your profile, open any rider's profile and see their picture full size, and share to Facebook, Instagram or X. Seeing the Feed, reading comments and liking are free; posting, commenting and sharing are part of Pro.

Events: rallies, poker runs and ride weekends on one page you can share, with dates, the place, photos, details and an agenda. Say you're Going or Interested, and join the event's group rides. Pro riders create events and can add co-hosts and Ride Managers who run each group ride.

Not sure whether you need an event or a public ride? Tap Event or Public Ride? on Events, Find a Ride or either Create screen for a quick explanation. Events also has a gold card on Home so it's easier to spot.

Invite Friends, under You > Settings. Share your invite link with a rider who's new to OnMyLead. When they finish their first ride, you both get Pro Annual for $14.99 your first year instead of $29.99. On iPhone and iPad it's an App Store offer code, filled in for you; on Android it's a Google Play offer. Already paying for Pro on Google Play? Your next bill moves back 6 months instead.

Navigate is now Map Mode, with its own blue button in the middle of the tab bar so your offroad map is one tap from any tab. Map a Custom Trail from the Draw tab, turn on Track Line to see where you've been (one colour per day, kept 7 days on your phone only), and mark named spots like obstacles, hazards, water crossings and viewpoints that travel with the trail. Shared trails are now full length, with an optional Hide My Start for recordings.

Light mode and themes. Go to You > Appearance to pick Dark, Light or Match Phone, and one of four themes: Night Navy, Carbon (true black), Desert or Forest. Color Blind Mode switches rider status, trail and Track Line colors to ones that color blind riders can tell apart, and adds a symbol to riders who need a look.

A cleaner, calmer Ride Mode. The map gets the room: the ride name, sharing and the group's state sit in one slim bar, and the buttons sit in one dark panel with three quick replies, More for every status, and Regroup Here beside EMERGENCY. Announcements and alerts are easier to read, and every button gives a light tap you can feel.

Smoother live map. Rider dots glide to each new position instead of jumping, pins no longer flicker, and Follow Me moves the map in one steady motion. The map layers panel is now Map Style, with a picture of Satellite and Topo.

Type your own message in Ride Mode: tap Message, write a short line like "Gas stop at the next town" and tap Send to Everyone. It goes out like a quick reply, with the same Seen by lights and Cancel, and waits for signal if you have none. Check Save as One of My Quick Replies to send it again in one tap next time.

The leader line in Ride Mode now always has the leader at the far left and the tail gunner at the far right, with everyone else in order between them by how far back they are, on routes and Freerides. Your miles done and to go still show above the line.

The rider line on Freeride rides. With no mapped route, Ride Mode's line shows the leader at the far left, the tail gunner at the far right and every sharing rider in order between them, measured along the path the leader has ridden, so bends and switchbacks count. It shows how spread out the group is, from the leader to the tail gunner, and tells you how far ahead the leader is. The leader's path stays on your phone and isn't uploaded.

Notifications: tap the bell at the top right of the Rides tab to see what OnMyLead sent you in the last 30 days, with a red number for new ones. Tap one to open it, Mark All Read, swipe one left to clear it, or Clear All, which also clears them from your phone's own notification list and resets the app icon badge. Also on onmylead.com.

Follow Me: in Ride Mode and Map Mode the map now moves with you as you ride, so your dot stays in view without dragging the map. Drag or pinch the map to look around and it pauses; tap Paused or Center on Me to follow you again, or tap Following to turn it off. Your phone remembers the choice, and Follow Me on Maps in the You tab switches it too.

The keyboard could cover the box you were typing in when you commented on a post or wrote a direct message, so you couldn't see your words. The box now stays just above the keyboard on iPhone, iPad and Android, in comments, direct messages and group chat.

Your own dot had no direction arrow. Other riders' dots showed which way they were heading, but your own blue dot never did, because iPhone, iPad and Android draw that dot without a direction. Now your dot gets the same white arrow while you're moving.

A rider whose phone shares only a rough location could show up a mile or two from where they really were. Ride Mode now shows a banner when Precise Location is off, when Google Location Accuracy is off (Android), or when your phone's location is rough, and tapping it fixes it or shows how (including calibrating in Google Maps). On Android, OnMyLead also asks for both once when you start sharing.
Riders sharing a rough location show Approximate Location in the riders list, and Ride Bubble leaves out the distance their location could be off by, so a rider beside you isn't called separated.

Leave Ride is now at the bottom of the ride page whichever section you're on, and under the Riders list in Ride Mode (the Riders sidebar on a tablet). It always asks first, says what happens, and stops your phone sharing your location for that ride. Asked to join or on the waitlist? The same button says Withdraw.

Organizers can leave their own ride. Tap Leave Ride, pick who takes over from the riders who joined, and they become the organizer and leader. Nobody else on it yet? Leave Ride offers to cancel the ride instead.

Full Map on every map: Ride Mode, Map Mode, Draw a Route, Waypoints and Find a Ride. Tap Full Map and the bars and panels tuck away so the map fills your screen. One slim bar keeps what matters (EMERGENCY and the route line in Ride Mode, your speed in Navigate, the miles and Undo while drawing a route), and Controls brings everything back. Swipe the bar up to do the same. Your phone remembers it for next time.

OnMyLead now tells you when there's a newer version. An Update Available card shows at the top of the home screen once the update is in the App Store or Google Play. Tap Update to go straight to it, or close the card.

Music Controls: tap the Music button in Ride Mode or Map Mode to pause, skip songs and change the volume without leaving OnMyLead. On Android it controls Spotify, YouTube Music, Apple Music, Pandora and other music apps. On iPhone and iPad it controls Apple Music, and the volume of any app (Apple doesn't let apps skip Spotify songs). Don't want it? Tap Hide Music Button, or switch off Music Controls on the You tab.

Your ride summary, ride card and Mile Eater badge now count only the miles you actually rode. A phone with a rough location, GPS jumps, points left over from an earlier ride, or time with location off could add miles that weren't ridden: one short test ride showed about 60 miles. Those are now left out.

A Before You Ride screen on first launch: read the Rider Safety and Liability Agreement, tick the box and tap I Agree. You're asked once, and again only if it changes. Read it any time on the You tab under Safety Agreement.

On a Free account, a small gold Pro tag now marks every button that needs Pro, like Import GPX, Record a Trail, offline map downloads and New Group, so you know before you tap. Tap one to see what Pro adds. Pro Trial and Pro riders don't see the tags.

Report a Rider from the You tab. Pick anyone you've messaged, ridden with, added as a friend or blocked, and report them for harassment, threats or anything else. Your messages with them are saved with the report so the OnMyLead team can read what was said, and riders who break the rules can be suspended or banned. They're never told who reported them.

The Help Center's step-by-step guides are one tap away. On the You tab, Help now starts with Help Center: How-To Guides, and the Help and Support page opens with the same link and a Read the Guide link under each answer. The guides open right inside the app.
The Starlink page now features the RUS Starlink Mini Mount V2 (Morelock Series), made by RUS Offroad, the team behind OnMyLead. Tap Shop the Mount to see it in the store.

Waypoint symbols: pick from 15, including the new Gate, Trailhead, Water Crossing, Food, Restroom, First Aid, Repair and Photo Spot. Each has its own drawing and hazards sit on a triangle, so they're easy to tell apart for color-blind riders too. Planned stops show their symbol on the stop sign.

Trail width limits. Forest Service trails open only to ATVs and side-by-sides 50 inches or less now show a 50" Width Limit on their card, and any public trail can show the width other riders found. The card shows the middle of everyone's entries, so one wrong number doesn't change it.
Add Width Limit: tap a Forest Service, BLM or OpenStreetMap trail, tap Add Width Limit and type the narrowest gap in inches. Change or remove your own entry any time.
Add your machine's width in the Garage under Trail Fit. Trail cards, a trail's page and Plan a Group Ride on This Trail then say whether it fits or is too wide.
Planning a group ride on a trail with a width limit shows the limit on the Riding banner and adds it to the ride's instructions for everyone who joins.
Share My Location with a family link showed an error ("Property 'crypto' doesn't exist") on iPhone, iPad and Android, and no link was made. Family links work again.

Tilt meter and Crash Alert. A Tilt tile in Map Mode and Ride Mode shows your vehicle's roll and pitch, turning amber, then red, near your limits; tap it for a full tilt meter. Zero it for your phone mount, set your own warning angles and get a buzz (or a spoken angle) before a steep lean. In Ride Mode, Crash Alert watches for a hard hit or a rollover: a 30 second I'm OK countdown starts, and if you don't answer, your group gets an EMERGENCY alert with your location. It never calls 911. Find it all under You, Tilt and Crash Alert.

Brand Ambassador and OnMyLead Founder: two new badges OnMyLead gives. Ambassadors wear a blue patch and the Founder a red one with a flag on the summit. They show at the top of Badges, beside the rider's name, on the Feed and on their profile.

Sync Across Devices. Sign in with the same account on your iPhone, iPad, Android phone or tablet, or onmylead.com, and your settings follow you: map style, Follow Me, directions app, Appearance, voice, tilt warnings and more. Your Map Mode trails and their photos are backed up privately to your account, so they're in My Trails on every device. Offline Maps lists the areas you downloaded on your other devices so you can get them in one tap. You > Sync Across Devices shows when it last synced.
A new look for the OnMyLead logo, with RUS Offroad bigger and to the right of OnMyLead.

Map Mode could open zoomed out over the whole state, with Zoom In to See Trails, when your phone didn't have your location yet (most often on Android right after starting the phone). It now moves to you as soon as your location comes in, unless you've already moved the map yourself.

New Free and Pro plans. Joining a ride, following the leader, Ride Mode, ride chat and every safety feature stay free and unlimited on every device, and Map Mode is free for 8 hours a month (the clock never runs while you're on a group ride). Pro adds unlimited Map Mode, map layers, drawing routes, waypoints, directions, custom trails, saving and rating trails, Track Line, named spots, custom codes, your own messages, music controls, poll voting, the garage build sheet, sync, themes, voices, and OnMyLead on an iPad, an Android tablet and the website. A gold Pro tag marks each one on a Free account.

OnMyLead now speaks 12 languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi and Indonesian. It starts in your phone's language when it's one of them, and English when it isn't. Tap the flag at the top of Home (or You > Language) to switch, and your other devices switch too. Some newer screens are still in English while they're translated.

title: Navigate Offroad, Exact Rider Dots and Better Maps
intro: Navigate is a new offroad map for riding on your own: record and share your own trails, rate trails other riders mapped, and measure distances. Rider dots sit on each rider's exact position at every zoom, are easier to see and point the way each rider is heading. Ride Mode's route line shows every rider in running order, Full Map gives you the map with nothing in the way, and a new button brings the map back to you. Roads and trails show from farther out, ride times take a few taps, rides can be planned for 2027 and beyond, sharing can stay on until you turn it off, and any sheet swipes down to close. New badges and ranks reward the rides you lead, join and finish, Out Riding shows which riders are out near you so you can message them, you can add riders as friends, and you can pick your own easy-to-say code for a ride, group or friend link.
whatsNew:
What's new in 1.0.3:

• Nav Mode: offroad map and your own trails.
• Badges and ranks for leading, riding and miles.
• Out Riding + Friends: see who's out and message them.
• Rider dots stay put and show heading.
• Full Map; riders in order on the route line.
• Ride Mode opens on you; Center on Me.
• Trails show from farther out.
• Faster time picker; plan rides in 2027+.
• Share location until you turn it off.
• Swipe down to close any sheet.
• Emergency: hold Alert My Group.
• Update alerts.

notes.text: Navigate, an offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. See every trail and road with your speed and elevation, draw trails with the distance finder or record them, add photos, and keep them on your phone or share them with every rider with a name, difficulty and the vehicles that fit. Trails other riders shared show as mint dotted lines on every map (turn them off in Settings). Tap one to rate its quality and how accurate the line is; trails rated inaccurate are hidden and the mapper is told. With Pro, record and share your trails and turn any trail into a group ride's route; the map, measuring and ratings are free.

Badges and ranks. Earn Bronze, Silver and Gold badges for leading rides (Trail Boss), riding at the rear (Tail Gunner), riding with a group (Crew Rider), your miles (Mile Eater) and the trails you share and rate (Trailblazer, Mapmaker, Trail Scout). Your levels add up to a rank from Rookie to Legend. See them on the You tab, get a notification when you earn one, and spot each rider's top badge beside their name.

Out Riding. Heading out, or at a park for the weekend? Switch on Out Riding from the Groups tab to see which riders are out near you right now and roughly how far away they are (never where), then send them a message. By default only riders you've ridden with can see you; pick Everyone Nearby to meet anyone at the same park who chose the same. It's off until you switch it on and turns itself off.

Friends. Add the riders you ride with as friends from Friends on the Groups tab, from a ride's Going list, from Out Riding or from a conversation, or share your friend link with anyone. Friends see each other in Out Riding and can message any time. There's no search by name, and being friends never shares where you are.
Full Map in Ride Mode. Tap Full Map to hide the ride name, banners, buttons and riders list. A slim bar keeps the route line, EMERGENCY and Menus, which brings everything back.
A small arrow on each moving rider's dot shows which way they're heading, and it stays true when you turn the map. Stopped riders show a plain dot.

If an update ever has a problem, the app can tell you: an About This Version card on the home screen explains what's wrong, Update Available lets you know a fix is out, and Please Update OnMyLead asks you to update (with Not Now, so you're never locked out on the trail).
Ride Mode has a Center on Me button. Tap it to bring the map back to your location. It keeps your zoom, and zooms in to riding distance if you were zoomed far out.
Share your location until you turn it off. Until I Turn It Off no longer stops after 24 hours, and ride shares get the same choice (they still end when the ride ends).
Pick an End Date when you share your location: choose a day and time up to a year out.

Pick your own code. Give your ride, riding group or friend link a code that's easy to say at the trailhead, like MOAB-2026, when you create it or later with Choose Your Own Code. The app checks as you type that nobody else uses it.

Profile pictures. Take a photo or choose one from your library on the You tab (tap your name). It's cropped square and shows next to your name in rider lists, chat, Messages, Friends and Out Riding, for signed-in riders only. No picture? You keep your initial.

The route line in Ride Mode shows every sharing rider's dot in running order, rear to front, and riders bunched together line up side by side instead of hiding each other. The leader is blue, the tail gunner purple, and you red. Tap a dot for the rider's name and place.
Rider dots are easier to see on satellite, topo and the dark map: each rider is a bold white ring with a dark name tag, and the leader is a bigger solid blue dot with a blue name tag.
Pick times by tapping instead of typing: tap AM or PM, the hour and the minute. Works for Meet At, Departure Time, Expected Finish, a planned stop's time and Stop Sharing At.

Swipe down to close any sheet: a new waypoint, Riders, Directions, Share Your Location, Emergency, a report, the Pro prompt and the ride's QR code. In a long sheet the first swipe scrolls back to the top, and if the keyboard is up it puts the keyboard away first.
Roads and dirt trails show on the Ride Mode map from about 15 miles across, so you no longer have to zoom way in to see them. When you're zoomed far out, the longest trails are drawn first.
Create a Ride takes dates in 2027 and later, up to three years out. On the calendar you can type a date or jump straight to any month and year.
The You tab shows your active location share and when it ends.

Rider dots in Ride Mode now sit on each rider's exact position and stay there as you zoom in and out. Before, every dot was drawn a little to the right of the rider, so riders who were together looked spread out. Waypoints, planned stops and search pins are placed exactly too.

Emergency in Ride Mode: Alert My Group now fills a bar while you hold it and says Keep Holding, so it no longer looks like nothing happens. A quick tap tells you the alert was not sent, and the screen closes as soon as the alert goes out so you can see who has it.
Trail and road lines no longer flash or disappear while you move or zoom the map.
Tablets show trails at the same zoom as phones. They used to appear only when zoomed in much closer.
Opening Help and Support, Contact Us, Terms or Privacy no longer shows an "Expo Head" alert.

Ride Mode's map opens centered on you, zoomed in close enough to see nearby trails, instead of over a random spot. If your phone is still finding you, the map centers as soon as it does, unless you've already moved it.

title: Android, Battery Saver and Trail Names
intro: OnMyLead arrives on Android phones and tablets. This update also adds Battery Saver, a ride calendar, Report a Bug, and trails that are easier to read.
whatsNew:
What's new in 1.0.1:

• Battery Saver: choose how often your phone sends its location while you share.
• Create a Ride has a calendar: pick any day up to a year out.
• Trails are bolder, show their names, and closed trails are marked in red.
• Search for a place on the waypoints map.
• Report a Bug from the You tab, with a screenshot.
• Ride Mode tells you when location is turned off for OnMyLead.

notes.text: OnMyLead is on Google Play for Android phones and tablets, with the same rides, live map, chat and Pro plan as on iPhone and iPad.
Battery Saver on the You tab lets you choose how often your phone sends its location while you share: Best Accuracy, Balanced or Max Battery Saver.
Create a Ride has a Calendar button to pick any day from today up to a year out, plus Sat and Sun quick picks for the coming weekend.
Report a Bug on the You tab sends us your message with a screenshot, your phone model and app version, so problems get fixed faster.
Trails are bolder and easier to see, with trail and road names on the map. Closed roads and trails, including today's seasonal closures, show in red with a Closed note.
Search for a park, trailhead, town or address on the waypoints map, the same way as in the route builder.
If you turn off location for OnMyLead while sharing, Ride Mode now tells you with a Location Is Off notice instead of saying you're still sharing.

title: First Release
intro: The first OnMyLead: plan a ride, bring your crew, and keep everyone together on one live map.
whatsNew:
Welcome to OnMyLead, the group ride app.

• Create a ride with a meeting point, time and route.
• Invite riders with a link, code or QR code.
• See your group on one live map in Ride Mode.
• Share your location only for the ride, and stop anytime.
• Ride chat, status buttons, polls and Ride Bubble alerts.
• Draw routes; with Pro, import GPX and save offline maps.
• Find rides near you and follow leaders.
• Works on iPhone and iPad.

notes.text: Create a ride with a meeting point, time, route and who can join, then share it with a link, code or QR code.
Ride Mode puts the whole group on one live map, with status buttons, ride chat, polls and Ride Bubble alerts when someone falls behind.
Location sharing is per ride and temporary. Your exact location is never public, and you can stop sharing anytime.
Draw a route and add waypoints and planned stops. With Pro, import GPX files and save maps for offline use.
Find a ride near you and follow leaders you ride with. With Pro, keep your regular crew together in a riding group with its own chat.
Free lets you create one ride a month and join as many as you like, with every safety feature included. Pro adds unlimited rides, offline maps, GPX import and riding groups, with a 30-day free trial.
iPad gets its own layouts: the live map with a riders sidebar, and split views for rides and routes.
